script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. ARTHUR MILLER CENTER - DAY

A bustling HUB of contemporary ART and LITERATURE, filled with the clamor of scholars, students, and professors.

A MATURE WOMAN in her mid-50s, ANGELA WEST (formerly an acclaimed PLAYWRIGHT), watches as her younger CO-WORKER, EMMA RICHARDS, sets up a booth for an upcoming literature festival.

ANNOUNCER (V.O.)
(Excitedly)
...and joining us for the first time, the esteemed Dr. Angela West!

INT. ARTHUR MILLER CENTER - ANGELA'S OFFICE - LATER

Angela sits at her desk, surrounded by piles of unread manuscripts and a half-finished play. Her phone RINGS. She hesitates before answering.

ANGELA
(Sighs)
Hello, Michael.

MICHAEL (V.O.)
Angela, I was hoping you could meet me at the café after work.

ANGELO
I don't think that's a good idea, Michael.

MICHAEL (V.O.)
We need to talk. About us.

Angela looks away, her eyes filling with tears.

ANGELA
I thought we were past this, Michael.

INT. ARTHUR MILLER CENTER - CAFETERIA - NIGHT

Angela meets MICHAEL KANE (her EX-HUSBAND, also a former acclaimed PLAYWRIGHT), who looks more disheveled and older than when she last saw him.

ANGELA
(Tentatively)
Michael, we've been through this. We both know it's over.

MICHAEL
(Desperately)
I know, but I need your help. I've hit rock bottom.

Angela hesitates, then leans in to listen.

INT. ARTHUR MILLER CENTER - ANGELA'S OFFICE - DAY

Emma enters, excitedly carrying a fresh manuscript.

EMMA
Angela, you won't believe the manuscript I just got! It's amazing!

Angela, distracted by her encounter with Michael, barely listens.

EMMA
(Noticing Angela's distracted demeanor)
Is everything okay?

Angela hesitates, then decides to share her encounter with Michael.

ANGELA
I ran into Michael at the café last night. He's a mess. He begged for my help.

Emma looks sympathetic.

EMMA
I know how hard it is to deal with your past. But maybe this is your chance for a second chance, not just for him, but for yourself.

INT. ARTHUR MILLER CENTER - LECTURE HALL - NIGHT

Angela and Michael share the stage for a joint lecture, their old sparks rekindling as they discuss their works and their lives.

MICHAEL
(Smiling)
You know, Angela, I've always admired your ability to create such compelling, complex characters.

Angela smiles back, her eyes shining with pride.

ANGELA
And I've always admired your ability to captivate an audience with your words.

INT. ARTHUR MILLER CENTER - ANGELA'S OFFICE - DAY

Angela sits at her desk, typing away at a new play, inspired by her rekindled relationship with Michael and the second chance they have been given.

INT. ARTHUR MILLER CENTER - LITERATURE FESTIVAL - DAY

Angela and Michael, now collaborating on a new play, take the stage to present their work to a packed audience. Their passion and love for their craft shine through, reminding everyone that no matter how many chances we are given, it's never too late to create something beautiful.

FADE OUT.
